title: Helps with ADHD but you eventually Catch Up
content:
Focus@Will – the ADHD brain’s equivalent of a zen garden… until my neurons learned the soundtrack. As a lifetime subscriber who happily traded cash for calm in my squirrel-powered mental circus, I’ll forever salute this app for being the first to successfully cage my distractible gremlins. For years, its science-y beats worked like a cognitive straitjacket – until my rogue hippocampus started Shazam-ing the background tracks.
Now when familiar rhythms surface, my focus transforms into a one-brain Broadway show: Is that a 60bpm delta wave mix or the opening number to “Attention: The Musical”? Tragically, my flow state now moonlights as a drumline critic.
While I’d still recommend it to anyone whose mind resembles a browser with 427 open tabs, the app’s two-year update hiatus has me wondering if developers ghosted us harder than my executive function at tax time. Five stars for past glory, only three for present reality, and a standing offer to beta test if they ever remember their App Store password.

title: Opportunities for Enhancement on Apple M3 Max Compatibility
content:
In exploring the capabilities of Focus@will on the latest Apple M3 Max, I've encountered some issues that, while frustrating, present opportunities for significant improvements. Firstly, the app seems incompatible with the new M3 Max architecture; notably, it lacks an accessible volume control, and more critically, fails to play music directly within the app. This necessitates a workaround of visiting the website to use the service, which, while a temporary fix, detracts from the seamless experience one would expect.

The absence of these fundamental functionalities hinders the utility and appeal of Focus@will for users who rely on the latest technology to enhance their productivity. It's paramount for an app, especially one designed to aid concentration and productivity, to ensure reliability and ease of use across all supported devices.

Addressing these issues not only will improve user satisfaction but also extend the app's reach to a broader audience, leveraging the full potential of the hardware advancements offered by the Apple M3 Max. It's an opportune moment for the developers to refine the app's compatibility and functionality, thereby reinforcing its commitment to providing an exemplary user experience.

title: The same handful of tunes on endless repeat
content:
I’ve been using this for years. Or at least, I did use it for years. The problem is that the “thousands of hours” of music that F@W boasts actually consists of multiple numbered remixes of the same few tracks. The whole point (or part of it, anyway) of using this type of music to focus if you have ADHD is that the music should be unfamiliar. At this point it’s been probably two years since I opened this app, but I can still “hear” a bunch of those tracks in my head. They become instantly recognizable so that you know them note for note. It has a feature that lets you tell it not to play certain tracks (specifically to avoid the “familiarity” thing), but when that track is just one of many indistinguishable iterations of the same thing, that feature is useless.

It’s a shame, because while this worked for me, it *really* worked. But that was… 2018? 2019? and (although they did put out a limited amount of additional music a couple of years back) they’re still using basically the exact same tracks. Not to mention that the app hasn’t seen an update in a year.

So - F@W is great for a short period or for *extremely* infrequent use, but that lifetime subscription didn’t pan out quite how I hoped it would.

If developer can address those issues which I consider to be basic, I’d give this app 5 stars all day every day.

You can imagine my shock when that was a $53/year subscription instead of a $3/week subscription like most other apps. Also what am I paying the $53 for?? The app has a lot to offer but it has much more to improve on before it starts changing people $53 a year in a pandemic where people have lost their jobs. Or that I got charged the normal price when I should have been charged around $20? Either way that’s too much to pay for this app. I think you would have much more success if you made the app more affordable or offer a longer trial than 7 days. I’ll continue to use the app until my subscription ends but I refuse to give the app 5 stars when it can be tricky to navigate, gets touchy, and costs more than most of the productivity apps in the App Store. Please reconsider your pricing tactics.

title: I think you could get more for money in app?
content: So, let’s start this off by saying I am invested in this app enough to pay for a subscription. I am an adult in academia and have been diagnosed with ADD. Toggling between tasks and managing several aspects of my career make it difficult for me to focus on research and paper writing- elements essential to my career. On top of it all, i have a cubicle in a shared office space room and it is so easy to lose focus and get distracted from deep work. I got interested in this app after a Reddit suggestion, read about it, and was interested in the evidence- and research-based aspect. I’ve found that certain music in this app really does help boost my productivity. I gave it four stars because the whole concept is very helpful but it could be better. I also don’t normally write reviews, but I’m going to pay for the subscription and now I’m invested to see this get better. So, I’m writing this in hopes the developers take some suggestions to heart. Since this is also a data-driven app, my suggestions could be possible to implement. First, it would be helpful to see number of productivity sessions each day in a bar chart. Second, it would be helpful if the developers allowed space for users to record what they worked on during the productivity session. For example, # words written. It might also be helpful to have a smiley face for users to click on to indicate how they felt. This goes with years on productivity diaries for academic writing, but could be applied to other fields. At the minimum, it is helpful that we can record percent of productivity so that this could be applied to all workers, but it’d be nice if there were more specific work tracking options. Third, when my phone gets interrupted, such as with a phone call, the tracking stops. Please program this so that this partial session was recorded. In conclusion, my take is that if you are going to spend almost $100/year on this, more data tracking elements could be incorporated into the app.

title: Useful, but poor value for money
content:
If F@W cost $7.99 or less, I’d happily give five stars to the app as-is. It does help me focus!
However, it’s just not robust enough to justify its subscription price. 

At $12.99, the price is extravagant, one of the most expensive subscription apps I have ever seen. 
It costs more than a Spotify subscription! Except unlike Spotify, this is a single-function app with very basic features. At that price, I have to consider how much value I get out F@W versus “focus” playlists on Spotify, YouTube mixes, and free or low-priced study music apps.

At the current price, it needs improvement in AT LEAST the following features:

1. OFFLINE MODE - 

$12.99 a month and there’s not even an offline mode? So I have to pay for data on top that? I’m in a coffee shop with terrible WiFi, and F@W is almost unusable. This would be acceptable at a very low subscription price, but ridiculously annoying as is. For $12.99. I shouldn’t be restricted in using the app!

2. MORE VARIETY - 
There aren’t that many stations to choose from, and not all of them will work for you, so you end up using only a small subset. Mode stations would at least make it feel like you are getting some value for your money. 

3. MORE & BETTER RECOMMENDATIONS -
The marketing makes F@W’s service seem way more personalized than it actually is.
The channel recommender quiz is a nice idea in theory, but it is TOTALLY USELESS to me. It recommends a station for the “type of person” you are, and of course your inherent attributes don’t change. If the recommendation doesn’t work for you (mine didn’t at all), too bad, I guess.
The marketing references music tailored for “creative thinkers”, “logical thinkers”, “entrepreneurs”, and “students”. Based on that, I expected a much more robust recommendation system. People wear different “hats” depending on the task they are doing, and I expected to receive recommendations tailored to that.
I expected F@W to tailor recommendations for creative tasks (writing, design), logical tasks (coding), reading, etc. 

This app is quite basic in its currently form and there’s really no way to justify charging $12.99.

Yes, it is useful and improve focus. I’m loving the functionality that this app provides for my life, but I can’t justify keeping my subscription when I can accomplish something similar for free.

title: What can I say?
content: Before Focus, I was short, fat, and bald. Now with Focus, I'm tall, lean, and have a full head of hair. But really, I did the trial a while back, and opted not to pay. Then, heard it mentioned again on a podcast, decided not to be cheap and go with a paid subscription. It wasn't easy as I had listened to podcasts all day and I still miss my podcasts but I definitely feel that it's made great improvements on my ability to focus. I set the timer for 35 minutes and do my best to stand there and work. I have a standing desk. Ok, so do the trial, and if you can afford it, just go with the paid subscription and test out the various sounds to find the one that works for you as some I love and others I totally hated. And sometimes I'll switch up just for a change of pace. Get Focus and you'll be better able to focus if you can only get that person in the cubicle next to you to shut up about Trump.

title: It pays for itself many times over every day.
content:
I measured my productivity with focus@will vs playing other music in background. F@W is hands down winner. It is better than pomadoro apps because the music is geared toward work and constantly changing so it does not become familiar. Better than just background music because no fiddling around looking for what I want to hear. I don’t really “hear” F@W per se, it just plays and masks distractions. 

Why four stars vs five?  I play it on iPad linked via Bluetooth to a nice stereo system.  There is no volume control on the iPad user interface so a conversation with a client causes me to go fumbling around for volume button on edge of iPad.  Also - it would be extremely useful to know how many complete sessions I have accomplished during the day. For example, a number displayed on the UI saying 9 would tell me I got in 9 sessions so far today.

title: Amazingly helpful. Truly delivers
content:

I use this app any time I need to focus and be productive. It really calms me and lets me be my best productive self. I find I am not only more productive but that the quality of my work improves. 
I can also share a funny story about my teenage son. He had a report due by midnight one day. He "worked" on it all day getting no where. Finally at 10pm I lost it and decided I would sit in the room with him until he finished. Again no focus!(he has ADHD). Finally out of desperation I pulled out this app and played the music. He fought with me that he did want to hear it, etc.  Comically within 10 minutes he was turned towards his computer and writing. It was like a switch had been flipped. He wrote for 1.5 hours straight and turned in his paper on time. Now he asks for "that" music when he needs to get things done.

Secondly the app will occasionally "fail to load" which means you cannot access any audio. I have no idea why this occurs so frequently - usually requires you to force restart the app a few times, even on wifi where the connection is rather good. Finally I would suggest tweaking the productivity factor tracking. This is largely a user input process, but the options are in quartiles and sometimes I am feeling between 75% and 100% focused. I would suggest perhaps seeing how many times the user switches out of the app (answering texts, browsing the web) for a true measure of productivity. 

Those criticisms aside, this is a nice (albeit expensive) app to have. The existing competition is limited.

title: Lifesaver! No offline-mode is its only flaw
content:
I am at the end of my free trial and–wow!! I have major anxiety and ADHD/ADD. I have so many ideas and it is always a struggle to stick to an idea and develop it (i.e. writing papers). This, along with timers, has really decreased that struggle. I also live with my mother (I am a young adult), who talks out of anxiety incessantly, and I play this when she stifles me with her repetitive ramblings to drown her out and to self-soothe myself. 

What is surprising to me is that normally classical music makes me fidgety, but here I can enjoy its beauty with out anxiety. This really makes me want to research the scientific research behind this app, because whatever they have modified in the classical music works for me (I believe they have modified the classical music, but have yet to do a side-by-side comparison to other sources of the tracks, so this is not definitive). Also, the ADHD mode (the primary mode I use) is music with a fast tempo, which is a surprise for me but has been the key. It lets me ride out the wave of ny anxieties and discursiveness.

With this app, I have access to a retreat in the palm of my hands, in the middle of a squirmy, noisy, lively, icky, golden city; this app is my home-base among this flitting, inconsistent city. And, more profoundly, it overthrows the flitting, inconsistency of my mind normally reigned by rumination and anxiety.

Some unique features: an option among three different intensity modes for each type of music; and a cinematic mode (never thought of this as a possible music genre, but when you hear it you will see that it is mot juste). 

Now, this would get 5 stars ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ IF it had an offline mode. I live in a huge, noisy city and would love to use this while on the subway, where I spend a good 10% of my out-and-about waking life. 

Thank you focus@will!

title: I enjoy F@W, but this app seems redundant
content:
As an early beta tester I've been using the F@W online music player since the beginning. I was excited when the iOS app launched, but after trying it out for a while I'm not really sure why it even exists. What I mean by that is: A) the majority of links / buttons within the app simply launch the mobile Safari app and load a page from the F@W website (which actually gets pretty annoying after the first 3-4 times); and B) the app doesn't seem to offer anything that isn't already available on said site. 

Whereas, if I use F@W on mobile Safari instead of the app, at least it won't keep opening up another application.

So I guess my question is: what's the purpose of this app? What do users gain by installing another 10MB app vs simply using the mobile website?

title: Really Does Help Focus
content:
Update:  The App stability has deteriorated badly.  It is virtually unusable as a focus aid despite the neuroscience.  I purchased a one year subscription and will cancel if it can not be fixed soon.  The company did reach out and were very professional and concerned with fixing the problems.  I assume they are working on fixing, but it needs a patch and some redesign quickly.  I can not even listen to a 100 minute session without it disconnecting midway about 50% of the time.  Productivity tracker no longer works.

Best focus app I have ever tried, but the App itself is too buggy.  Crashes, stops playing, productivity tracker  does not initiate after session ends.  Also, does not multitask well: If you are using another app while it is playing, it will not initiate the productivity tracker after the session ends, and sometimes the session will end before the time setting for the session. Also, very annoying start up not on landscape mode. Can change to landscape mode only after the player connects with the music service, and then you have to turn your iPad up and down several times before it finally sets in landscape mode. Once all of these bugs are fixed, it will really be a great attention, focus app. I did buy a subscription because the music sessions really helps me focus and concentrate. Can use a little more variety for each genre.
